result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A's diagram labels every stage, including Feed, directly in the chart. It places 'Best time to mix dough' at the peak and uses no hour counts at all ('Hours, not minutes', 'Many hours later'), so it never risks false precision. B has a clear hour axis and a caveat about temperature and feeding ratio, but its stage cards still give hour ranges. B's curve also has an odd uptick at the end, and the '1 · Fed' and 'sinks' labels crowd the line. A has one small flaw of its own: its collapse caption slightly overlaps the curve. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both pages pair a clear rise-and-fall SVG with stage labels drawn on the diagram and four stage cards, in a restrained dark palette. B is slightly better: it puts 'Best time to mix dough' inside the peak band and uses no hour figures at all, so nothing reads as a universal rule. A uses a 12-hour axis and per-stage hour ranges; it does add a 'your hours will differ' caveat, but the 'Hour by Hour' title pushes toward false precision. Both have small cases of annotation text overlapping the curve.
